docs.title: DORAI AI
docs.text:
An open-source AI assistant with persistent memory that runs on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Get Started GitHub

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: DORAI AI is built with Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform. It connects to 30 LLM providers (plus a keyless Free tier and on-device models) with automatic fallback, remembers important details across conversations, and can act autonomously via scheduled heartbeats and tool execution.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Persistent memory — DORAI AI remembers important details across conversations and uses them automatically
  • Customizable soul — Define the AI's personality and behavior with an editable system prompt
  • Multi-service fallback — Configure multiple providers; DORAI AI automatically tries the next one on failure
  • On-device inference — Run models locally with LiteRT on Android, iOS and desktop, no internet needed
  • Tool execution — Web search, notifications, calendar events, shell commands, and more
  • MCP server support — Connect to remote tool servers via the Model Context Protocol
  • Interactive UI — The AI can answer with interactive screens (forms, buttons, multi-step flows) instead of plain text
  • Skills — Install reusable instruction bundles in the SKILL.md format (Android)
  • Autonomous heartbeat & scheduled tasks — Periodic self-checks plus one-time or recurring tasks the AI schedules
  • Linux sandbox — On Android, the AI can run shell commands, scripts and packages in a Debian or Alpine environment
  • DORAI Build — An Android coding environment with terminals and coding agents (Claude Code, Grok, OpenCode)
  • Encrypted storage — Conversations are stored locally with encryption
  • Settings export/import — Back up and restore all settings as a JSON file
  • Text to speech — Listen to AI responses
  • Image attachments — Attach images to any conversation

docs.title: Hybrid Development
docs.text:
DORAI AI keeps Kotlin Multiplatform as its primary application platform and provides a separate TypeScript workspace for future browser-facing modules and integrations. The workspace does not replace Compose or the existing Kotlin/Wasm target.

docs.title: Audit rules
docs.text:
• A source file is not considered migrated merely because it imports DesignTokens.
  • Review visible Composables and their states: idle, loading, empty, success, error, disabled, selected, expanded/collapsed, and confirmation.
  • Keep terminal ANSI palettes, diff semantics, and success/warning/error semantics where those colors are part of the content or state contract.
  • Do not change runtime, navigation, persistence, provider, MCP, sandbox, or permission behavior as part of visual-only migration.
  • Mark a surface complete only after source review and relevant screenshot/interaction coverage.

docs.title: Application ownership
docs.text:
• App.kt owns the application route shell and applies the selected Material color scheme to the root content.
  • Top-level routes: Home → ChatScreen; Dashboard → DashboardScreen; Settings → SettingsScreen; Build → KaiBuildScreen.
  • Sandbox is embedded in Chat/Build workspace flows, not a top-level route.
  • Phase A1 source map: docs/2027-premium-ui-phase-a1-composable-map.md.

docs.title: Theme sources of truth — current state is inconsistent
docs.text:
File / symbol Current responsibility Audit finding ui/theme/DesignTokens.kt 2027 base palette, spacing, radius Static dark/OLED-oriented values; one global singleton ui/KaiAppTheme.kt Optional wrapper and LocalDesignTokens Injects static DesignTokens regardless of colorScheme/useOLED; not the observed persisted-mode adapter ui/Theme.kt Material schemes, typography, legacy palette, shapes, borders, modifiers 932-line mixed legacy/current theme file; mutable global KaiThemeColors plus CompositionLocal; multiple independent schemes ui/chat/ChatDesignTokens.kt Chat spacing/shapes/status/surface helpers Duplicates global spacing and shape values; surface helpers partly depend on Material scheme ui/settings/SettingsDesignTokens.kt Settings spacing/shapes/status/surfaces Duplicates global spacing/radii; colors mostly delegate to DesignTokens ui/build/BuildDesignTokens.kt Build spacing/shapes/status/surfaces/workspace tiers Duplicates spacing/radii; terminal-specific surfaces and build status mapping are legitimate domain tokens

The documented persisted theme contract in docs/design-system/theme-contract.md defines System, Light, Dark, Midnight and OLED Black. Midnight and OLED must remain distinct. Theme schemes also include branded/legacy alternatives (e.g. Lilac, Dusk, Seafoam, Graphite, Daybreak and provider-inspired palettes) in Theme.kt; before consolidating, all references and persisted settings must be traced. Do not remove a scheme or rename a persisted value as part of a visual refactor.

High-risk issue: KaiAppTheme currently provides the static DesignTokens object regardless of its selected ColorScheme and useOLED parameter. The active Theme path separately computes a legacy KaiColorPalette, mutates KaiThemeColors, then provides the same static DesignTokens. This can make components reading LocalDesignTokens disagree with Material light/OLED surfaces. Replace this with a mode-aware immutable token palette only after tracing all call sites and proving compatibility.

docs.title: P0 — theme correctness / compatibility
docs.text:
1. Reconcile DesignTokens, KaiColorPalette, KaiThemeColors, LocalKaiColors, and LocalDesignTokens into a single mode-aware token contract.
  2. Preserve all documented ThemeMode values and all still-referenced branded schemes.
  3. Remove mutable global theme state only after replacing all property getter consumers with composition-local reads; global mutable state is unsafe for previews, parallel compositions, and multi-window desktop.
  4. Make useOLED meaningful or remove it only after call-site and API compatibility review.
  5. Keep Material colorScheme, content colors, typography and shapes coherent with the same selected mode.

docs.title: P1 — duplicated primitives / inconsistent raw values
docs.text:
• ChatDesignTokens.kt: duplicate 2–48dp spacing scale, chat-specific shapes, fallback purple and semantic status mapping.
  • SettingsDesignTokens.kt: duplicate spacing/radii; retain settings-only layout constants (section/card gap) as feature aliases if needed.
  • BuildDesignTokens.kt: duplicate common spacing/radii; preserve terminal shape, ANSI/status mapping and workspace width breakpoints as domain-specific values.
  • Theme.kt: legacy global colors, shapes, borders, elevation helpers, card modifiers and text-field colors.
  • KaiDialog.kt: raw 16dp shape, 24/20dp padding and 16dp gaps should map to semantic dialog tokens.
  • SettingsListItem.kt: use shared spacing and shape aliases.
  • KaiSnackbar.kt: keep status-dependent colors semantic; consolidate only geometry.
  • Chat tool cards: ToolExecutionCard.kt general tool-call card already uses DesignTokens; preserve ShellExecutionCard terminal chrome, ANSI palette and window-control dots. ToolConfirmationCard.kt already uses semantic warning/error/success tokens and balanced action rows; review focus/disabled states before changing layout.
  • ModelSelectionSheet.kt: general surfaces already use DesignTokens; preserve score bands as domain semantics unless product design explicitly redefines them. Verify loading/empty/error/retry/selected states.
  • CodeFenceBlock.kt: hardcoded editor palette (#0A0E14, #161B22, #1E293B etc.) is a code-editor semantic palette; centralize as Markdown/code tokens, not generic brand surfaces.
  • DiffCard.kt: added/removed/hunk colors are semantic diff colors; centralize as DiffPalette tokens and preserve contrast. Do not recolor as cyan brand UI.
  • Terminal-specific ANSI colors, PTY cell metrics, terminal control dots and terminal canvas must remain isolated from generic theme migration.

docs.title: P2 — layout, typography and accessibility
docs.text:
• Audit all raw dp/sp and Material defaults in visible feature files; migrate only repeated visual primitives. Keep content-specific dimensions (terminal cells, icon sizes, chart/map dimensions, touch target constraints) explicit and documented.
  • Confirm font scale, long localized strings, keyboard focus, hover, selected/disabled semantics, minimum 48dp targets, reduced-motion and screen-reader labels.
  • Avoid changing interaction order, keyboard shortcuts, back handling, scrolling, state ownership, or accessibility role semantics in a visual-only change.

docs.title: 6. Known gaps / decisions required before source migration
docs.text:
1. KaiAppTheme.useOLED is currently not used to select tokens.
  2. LocalDesignTokens is static and cannot distinguish Light, Dark, Midnight or OLED.
  3. KaiThemeColors is mutable global state; all consumers must be inventoried before removal.
  4. Branded/provider-specific schemes in Theme.kt must be checked against persisted selection and UI references before deciding whether to keep, adapt or deprecate.
  5. Existing screenshot coverage is not a complete screen/state matrix. PremiumScreenScreenshotTest currently covers Dashboard dark, Build setup dark, tool execution running/failed dark, and pending tool confirmation dark.
  6. The visual regression matrix document already defines Light/Dark/Midnight/OLED and device-size expectations, but those expectations exceed current screenshot evidence.
  7. Existing coverage audit documents disagree in baseline commit/run references and have stale 137-file counts. Update them only after this new map is accepted as the current source of truth.
  8. No runtime visual inspection can be claimed from source reads or Paparazzi alone. Desktop/Android runtime and accessibility checks need their own CI/manual evidence.

docs.title: 7. Execution sequence
docs.text:
1. Finish read-only call-site inventory for theme mode, palette providers, raw legacy token references and all visible interactive states.
  2. Implement P0 theme contract first, with compatibility aliases and unit tests.
  3. Migrate shared primitives and feature token aliases (P1) in one controlled batch.
  4. Migrate screen surfaces and state visuals by feature; preserve all non-visual logic.
  5. Add screenshot coverage for missing state/theme/layout cells. Review intentional golden diffs; never blanket-accept.
  6. Run one CI workflow at a time. Wait for completion before creating another commit.
  7. After all required checks are green, remove only obsolete compatibility aliases, temporary bootstrap markers and superseded audit artifacts after verifying no references remain.
  8. Re-run targeted tests/CI after cleanup. Do not merge PR #11, release or deploy without separate approval.

docs.title: 8. Audit verdict
docs.text:
Audit status: implementation map established; source migration not yet started.

This document is the durable reference for where each change belongs and what must be preserved. It supersedes stale estimates only where its baseline and explicit inventory counts are newer. Phase A1's route-level composition map remains the authoritative route ownership reference.

No source/runtime behavior, navigation, persistence, provider, MCP, sandbox, terminal, permission, clipboard or URI behavior was changed during this audit.

docs.title: 6. Verified composition call-site trace (Phase A1 closure)
docs.text: The following call-site trace was checked against the current branch source, not inferred from file names:

docs.title: Chat route and responsive shell
docs.text:
• AppContent wraps NavHost in FullScreenImageHost; Home resolves to ChatScreen, Dashboard to DashboardScreen, Settings to SettingsScreen, and Build to KaiBuildScreen.
  • ChatScreen delegates to ChatScreenContent, then ChatModeScreen. ChatModeScreen owns local presentation state (drawer, sandbox visibility, composer prefill, snackbar/scroll state) while actions remain on ChatUiState.actions.
  • ChatModeScreen supplies ChatShell slots: TopBar as header; AppSidebar as the expanded conversation rail and compact modal drawer content; timeline/empty-state plus ChatComposer as main content; SandboxTabsContent as compact main content or expanded side panel; snackbar/error/free-provider UI in overlays.
  • ChatShell places header above content. Only Expanded width renders optional rail and side panel; Compact/Medium renders main content full-width. The caller owns the compact drawer and decides whether sandbox is shown.
  • Main-content branches verified: empty history -> EmptyState; non-empty history -> ChatTimeline; compact sandbox-open -> SandboxTabsContent replaces timeline/composer; composer is omitted while sandbox is open.

docs.title: Settings route and all tab branches
docs.text:
• SettingsScreen -> adaptive settings shell/navigation -> SettingsDetailPane.
  • Exact SettingsTab dispatch in SettingsDetailPane:
  • General -> SettingsOverview + GeneralContent (Android update slot is passed here).
  • Appearance -> AppearanceContent.
  • Agent -> AgentContent.
  • Services -> ServicesContent.
  • Tools -> ToolsTabContent (receives sandbox state).
  • Integrations -> IntegrationsContent.
  • Sandbox -> SandboxSettingsCard when sandbox UI is available; otherwise SandboxUnavailableContent.
  • Data -> DataControlContent.
  • Account -> AccountPlanContent.
  • Navigation rail labels/icons and grouping were checked against the same nine enum values in SettingsNavigation.kt. Groups: Assistant (General/Appearance/Agent), Models & services (Services), Connections (Tools/Integrations), Workspace (Sandbox), Account (Data/Account).

docs.title: Dashboard route
docs.text:
• DashboardScreen collects SandboxController and KaiBuildController state, builds DashboardUiState, then calls DashboardScreenContent.
  • DashboardScreenContent composes exactly: DashboardHeader -> ReadinessCard -> DashboardActionGrid -> RecentWorkSection.
  • RecentWorkSection conditionally shows conversation rows when conversations exist and project rows only when projects exist and Build is available. Grid columns are 1 below 600dp, 2 below 1000dp, and 4 otherwise.

docs.title: Build route
docs.text:
• KaiBuildScreen owns ViewModel collection/actions and delegates presentation to KaiBuildScreenContent.
  • With an open project: BuildSessionBar is shown; then Files -> SandboxFilesContent; else a matching/fallback session -> BuildTerminalContent; else a starting-session placeholder is shown and a session is requested.
  • Without an open project: KaiBuildTopBar is shown; ready state -> BuildProjectsContent; not-ready state -> BuildSetupContent. Create-project dialog is an overlay controlled by the screen.

docs.title: Sandbox embedded workspace
docs.text:
• ChatModeScreen is the verified call site for SandboxTabsContent in both compact and expanded layouts. Build also reuses SandboxFilesContent as its project file view.
  • Ready state: Terminal -> optional SessionChipRow + TerminalContent; Files -> SandboxFilesContent; Packages -> SandboxPackagesContent.
  • Not-ready state: setup card reports Needs setup / Installing / Failed, optionally shows progress/cancel or error, and offers setup/retry when not working.
  • The tab selection is session-backed when SandboxSessionViewModel exists, otherwise local state is used (e.g. preview).

docs.title: Markdown and Dynamic UI embedding
docs.text:
• MarkdownContent converts source text to a parsed MarkdownDocument (with a safe plain-text fallback) and delegates each block to BlockRenderer.
  • BlockRenderer dispatches headings/paragraphs/lists/quotes/tables/math/code/diff to their leaf renderers. A KaiUiBlock is the direct embedding point for KaiUiRenderer; malformed DORAI AI-UI JSON is rendered as a JSON code fence.
  • KaiUiRenderer recursively renders the typed KaiUiNode tree and passes callback data through its typed callback contract. Historical/read-only messages set isInteractive = false at the Markdown boundary.

docs.title: Platform and overlay ownership
docs.text:
• Top-level route set is commonMain NavHost; Android-only capability flags are passed from AppContent for Sandbox and DORAI Build. Android update UI is an optional slot passed through Settings -> General.
  • Full-screen image hosting is above NavHost. Chat snackbar/error/free-provider overlays are owned by the chat route; Settings dialogs/sheets are owned by Settings; Build create-project dialog is owned by Build; Sandbox progress/setup UI is inline within its embedded workspace.
  • Platform back handlers are attached to Dashboard, Settings, and Build route boundaries; Chat handles its own back/drawer/sandbox state.

docs.title: A1 coverage boundary
docs.text: This closes the route/feature-level composition map for all top-level routes and the cross-feature surfaces that materially affect the premium UI migration. It is not a line-by-line inventory of every private leaf composable invocation or every shared primitive consumer; those are implementation-detail references and are intentionally not represented as a false 100% exhaustive call graph. All 137 source files remain assigned to their owning feature in the inventory above. Visual/accessibility state coverage remains Phase C verification.

docs.title: 7. Phase A1 status
docs.text:
Status: Complete -> all top-level route roots, route ownership, responsive Chat slots, nine Settings tab branches, Dashboard composition, Build state branches, Sandbox tabs/readiness branches, Markdown -> Dynamic UI embedding, and major overlay/platform boundaries are source-verified.

The closure is scoped to route and feature-level composition; it does not claim a complete private-composable call graph or runtime visual verification. No runtime behavior, navigation, provider, persistence, MCP, sandbox, or permission logic was changed by this audit. No merge, release, or deployment is included.

docs.title: Phase B1 CI correction record
docs.text:
The CI run for the initial theme-token implementation identified: - A non-infix invocation of the Compose Color luminance extension in DesignTokens.kt. - Spotless import-order violations in Theme.kt and ThemeColorSchemeTest.kt.

Corrective commit: a9670bf60f018ab054a80a2522dea1b07a84c115.

The correction changes only the extension-call syntax and import ordering. It does not change theme mapping, persisted settings, UI behavior, or compatibility APIs.

Phase B2 remains blocked until all validation jobs pass.

docs.title: Phase B1 — Theme-scoped immutable color tokens
Change

• Added immutable DesignColorTokens roles for text, surfaces, cards and borders.
  • Added LocalDesignColorTokens, whose default preserves the existing dark design fallback.
  • The root Theme(colorScheme) now derives and provides this palette from the exact Material 3 ColorScheme supplied to it.

docs.text:
• Existing DesignTokens spacing, radii, brand accents, semantic status colors and terminal background remain unchanged.
  • Existing LocalDesignTokens and KaiThemeColors APIs remain in place for this incremental migration.
  • Persisted ThemeMode values remain System/Light/Dark; no serialized preference or settings UI was changed.
  • This commit does not yet migrate feature consumers to LocalDesignColorTokens, nor remove the mutable compatibility singleton. Those require a separately audited, feature-batched migration.

docs.title: Phase C — Final Cleanup, Compatibility Removal & Regression Plan
docs.text: Date: 2026-11-02 Branch: feature/2027-premium-agent-ui-migration PR: #11 (Draft/Open) Baseline commit: latest on branch (post Phase B2 shared-component batch)

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
Phase C is the final cleanup and regression-verification phase that runs after: - Phase B1 (theme-scoped immutable DesignColorTokens + LocalDesignColorTokens) ✅ complete & CI green - Phase B2 consumer migration batches (shared components ✅ in progress; Chat, Settings, Dashboard, Build, Sandbox, DynamicUI, Markdown pending)

Phase C has two goals: 1. Remove obsolete compatibility APIs (KaiThemeColors, TextPrimary/TextSecondary/… getters, LocalKaiColors) only after zero references are confirmed across all source sets, tests, and previews. 2. Run the full regression matrix (theme, layout, screenshot, motion, accessibility) and declare migration complete only when every CI job is green.

No merge, release or deploy is performed in this phase.

docs.title: 3. Phase C audit checklist (read-only, must pass before removal)
docs.text:
Run these before any removal:

  1. Reference search across composeApp/src (all source sets), screenshotTests, and androidApp:
  2. KaiThemeColors
  3. LocalKaiColors
  4. TextPrimary / TextSecondary / TextTertiary / TextMuted (top-level getters, not DesignColorTokens fields)
  5. SurfaceElevatedTheme / CardSurfaceTheme / BorderStrongTheme (if any)
  6. @Preview functions referencing the above
  7. Confirm zero references in: commonMain, androidMain, iosMain, desktopMain, wasmJsMain, commonTest, desktopTest, androidApp, screenshotTests.
  8. Confirm temporary markers (RECORD_GOLDENS, bootstrap commits, // TODO migration markers) are absent or intentionally retained.
  9. Confirm no platform-specific references remain (especially desktopMain scrollbar and iOS/wasm stubs).

docs.title: 4. Phase C removal rules (only after audit passes)
docs.text:
• Remove KaiThemeColors object only if zero references (audit §3.1–3.2).
  • Remove TextPrimary/TextSecondary/TextTertiary/TextMuted global getters only if zero references.
  • Remove LocalKaiColors only if zero references.
  • Remove SurfaceElevatedTheme/CardSurfaceTheme/etc. only if zero references.
  • Keep DesignTokens (static) and LocalDesignTokens permanently.
  • Keep KaiTypography, KaiShapes, KaiBorders permanently.
  • Do not remove useOLED without a separate audit (tracked separately).
  • Each removal is a separate commit; run CI after each.

docs.title: 5. Phase C regression matrix (must be green)
docs.text: Category Required checks Theme/root System/Light/Dark follow correct ColorScheme; DesignColorTokens derived from Material scheme; persistence round-trip; invalid/missing value → System fallback; no mutable global palette leakage in concurrent composition; Android system bar appearance correct Chat empty/message/streaming/error/tool states (running/completed/failed), approval pending, expanded/collapsed; phone/tablet/desktop widths; keyboard visible Composer empty/draft/multiline, attachment, slash/skill menu, sending/stopping, disabled; narrow width, large font, focus traversal Model selection loading/loaded/selected/empty/provider error/retry/free badge/score bands; compact & wide Settings all 9 tabs, selected tab, scroll clipping, loading/error/unavailable; compact selector, 840dp rail, large font, Bengali/long labels Dashboard readiness, missing services, empty/recent conversations, projects; 1/2/4 columns Build setup/installing/progress/cancel/error, project list, active session, terminal, unavailable; phone/tablet/desktop Sandbox setup/installing/failed/retry, terminal, files, packages, find, replace confirmation; compact/wide + destructive confirmation Markdown headings/lists/tables/code/copy/diff/math/invalid fallback/streaming; long code, horizontal overflow, light/dark Dynamic UI valid/legacy/malformed/oversized/interactive/historical read-only; action enabled/disabled, error fallback Shared controls hover/focus/pressed/selected/disabled/error/loading; mouse/keyboard/touch; 48dp minimum Motion normal + reduced motion; verify infinite/looping animation policy Screenshots PremiumScreenScreenshotTest, KaiUiScreenshotTest, ScreenshotTest, MathScreenshotTest, store/tablet suites — intentional golden diffs reviewed, never blanket-accepted Spotless spotlessCheck green Tests common unit tests, desktop tests, Android FOSS compile + unit tests

docs.title: 6. Phase C execution sequence
docs.text:
1. Finish remaining Phase B2 feature batches (Chat → Settings → Dashboard → Build → Sandbox → DynamicUI/Markdown), one batch per commit, CI green after each.
  2. Run the full audit checklist (§3) and record reference counts in this doc (update §2.1).
  3. If zero references confirmed, remove obsolete APIs per §4, one removal per commit, CI after each.
  4. Remove temporary markers / obsolete artifacts (verify no references).
  5. Run one final CI workflow (all jobs green).
  6. Declare migration complete only after all jobs green. Do not merge PR #11, release or deploy without separate approval.

docs.title: 7. Safety constraints during Phase C
docs.text:
• Never weaken SSRF validation, shell allowlisting, Android network security, encrypted storage, backup exclusions or release-integrity checks.
  • Do not add dependencies/plugins to mask compile errors.
  • Do not modify source/build/config without explicit authorization (this doc is planning only).
  • One CI workflow at a time; wait for completion before next commit.
  • Preserve all pre-existing user edits; never reset/stash/overwrite unrelated files.
  • PR #11 remains Draft/Open; no merge/release/deploy.

docs.title: 2027 Premium UI — Theme Runtime Audit Addendum
docs.text: Branch: feature/2027-premium-agent-ui-migration Audited revision: 04438de6f94fcd5c1a646a78a5f9522872d5209e Scope: Read-only verification of theme mode persistence, runtime composition, legacy scheme references, and token consumers. Status: Audit correction; no application source changed.

docs.title: 1. Verified runtime contract (source takes precedence over stale docs)
docs.text:
The current implementation exposes exactly three persisted modes:

  • composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/data/AppSettings.kt: ThemeMode = System, Light, Dark.
  • Persistence key is theme_mode; setThemeMode stores mode.name and updates _themeModeFlow.
  • loadInitialThemeMode() parses the stored enum name and falls back to System for missing or invalid values.
  • composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/App.kt: AppContent observes themeModeFlow; System resolves against isSystemInDarkTheme(), Light selects the supplied light scheme, Dark selects the supplied dark scheme. The resulting scheme is passed to Theme(colorScheme = effectiveColorScheme).
  • androidApp/src/main/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/MainActivity.kt: system-bar icon/style calculation currently maps System and Light through system appearance, and Dark to dark UI. This is a separate platform edge-to-edge calculation and must be kept consistent with the actual selected scheme.
  • GeneralSettings.kt: picker currently presents only System, Light and Dark.
  • SettingsUiState.kt, SettingsActions.kt, SettingsViewModel.kt, DataRepository.kt, RemoteDataRepository.kt, and FakeDataRepository.kt carry the same enum through settings state and persistence.

Correction: docs/design-system/theme-contract.md and docs/features/appearance.md describe Midnight and OLED Black, but these modes are not represented in the current ThemeMode enum, settings picker, App runtime switch, or Android system-bar switch. Do not implement those modes or assume they are persisted without an explicit product decision and a migration plan. Current runtime truth is System/Light/Dark.

docs.title: 2. Theme composition and token divergence
docs.text:
• ui/Theme.kt defines KaiColorPalette, LocalKaiColors, and mutable singleton KaiThemeColors.
  • Theme(colorScheme) infers light-vs-dark from colorScheme.background.luminance(), constructs a KaiColorPalette, copies every field into mutable KaiThemeColors, then provides LocalKaiColors and LocalDesignTokens.
  • The LocalDesignTokens provider currently supplies the static singleton DesignTokens, independent of the selected Material scheme.
  • ui/KaiAppTheme.kt also provides static DesignTokens. Its useOLED argument is currently unused. The wrapper is not the root persisted-mode adapter used by App.kt.
  • LocalKaiColors has no discovered consumer outside its definition/provider in Theme.kt; the global compatibility getters (TextPrimary, TextSecondary, TextTertiary, TextMuted, and theme-suffixed surface/border getters) are used broadly.
  • KaiTypography, KaiShapes, and KaiBorders are defined in Theme.kt; they are independent shared primitives and must not be deleted as part of the color-state migration.

docs.title: 3. Search-backed consumer inventory
docs.text:
GitHub code search on the audited branch returned these consumer groups:

  • TextPrimary: at least 50 matching files in the result window, spanning shared components, chat, settings, build, dashboard, sandbox, Markdown, and dynamic UI. This is a broad compatibility surface; migrate by bounded feature batches, not a blind replacement.
  • TextSecondary: at least 48 matching files across the same feature areas.
  • TextTertiary: 6 matching files.
  • TextMuted: 3 matching files.
  • DesignTokens: at least 33 matching files, including shared components, chat, settings, build, sandbox, dashboard and tests.
  • KaiShapes: at least 27 matching files.
  • KaiBorders: 5 matching files.
  • LocalDesignTokens: direct consumers include KaiSearchField.kt, ConversationRail.kt, AppSidebar.kt, and ChatScreen.kt; provider/default and tests also reference it.
  • No direct LocalKaiColors.current consumer was returned by code search; it is still part of the theme provider API and should be checked by a complete branch search before removal.
  • Theme-suffixed getters such as SurfaceElevatedTheme, SurfaceRaisedTheme, CardFillTheme, CardSurfaceTheme, and border variants currently resolve through KaiThemeColors and are only found in Theme.kt in the search result. Confirm via repository-wide search before removing them.

The search result count is a bounded search result window, not a mathematically complete total of symbol occurrences. The file paths are a practical migration inventory; verify exact references again immediately before deleting compatibility APIs.

docs.title: 4. Scheme definitions vs active runtime
docs.text: Theme.kt defines additional named palettes including Lilac, Dusk, Seafoam, Graphite, Daybreak and Carbon. Search found no corresponding persisted enum values or settings picker options. Some are imported into App.kt; before deleting or retaining them as supported themes, inspect all imports, call sites, previews and screenshot fixtures. Their existence alone does not establish user-selectable runtime support.

docs.title: 5. Test gap and required implementation tests
docs.text:
Current ThemeColorSchemeTest.kt contains tautological Light/Dark assertions (each compares a literal color with itself), checks static token constants, and verifies only that the CompositionLocal object exists. It does not verify runtime selection, token/scheme coherence, persistence round-trips, or Android system-bar mode mapping.

Before removing compatibility state, add behavior tests for: 1. System mode resolves to the supplied platform scheme under both system-light and system-dark. 2. Light and Dark resolve to the correct supplied schemes. 3. The CompositionLocal token palette matches the selected scheme and preserves semantic text/status/border roles. 4. Invalid/missing persisted enum values safely fall back to System; existing stored System/Light/Dark values remain readable. 5. Parallel compositions/previews cannot leak palette values through global mutable state. 6. KaiAppTheme(useOLED = ...) call sites are inventoried; preserve source compatibility or explicitly deprecate the unused argument only after proving no external API requirement. 7. Android system-bar style remains correct for all supported modes.

docs.title: 6. Implementation guardrails
docs.text:
• Do not add Midnight/OLED modes as a side effect of the token refactor; first reconcile the stale docs with the intended product contract.
  • Preserve the three current serialized enum names and the theme_mode key.
  • Derive the immutable token palette from the same effective ColorScheme used by MaterialTheme.
  • Replace global getters with composition-local reads in controlled batches; do not remove them until all source, tests, previews and platform source sets have zero references.
  • Keep semantic status, code editor, diff, Markdown and terminal/ANSI palettes distinct from brand/surface tokens.
  • Keep KaiTypography, shape semantics, focus, selected/disabled states, touch targets, navigation and all business behavior unchanged.
  • The useOLED parameter is presently unused; do not infer that an OLED theme exists in runtime.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: P0-A addresses critical security findings identified in the read-only audit. All changes are security hardening — no feature changes, no branding changes.

docs.title: Phase 1: Backup (Completed)
docs.text:

  • Recovery branch: backup/pre-p0-20261019-014057
  • Working tree was clean before backup; no file modifications to preserve

docs.title: 1. Android Network Security Config
docs.text: File: androidApp/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml Change: Restricted cleartext HTTP to localhost only (localhost, 127.0.0.1, 10.0.2.2). Removed global cleartext allowance and user certificate trust. Impact: Cloud provider traffic (all HTTPS) unaffected. Self-hosted servers on LAN IPs require HTTPS or tunnel. Risk: Medium — users with LAN self-hosted servers may need to reconfigure.

docs.title: 2. Android Backup Disable
docs.text: File: androidApp/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml Change: allowBackup="true" → allowBackup="false" Impact: No ADB/cloud backup of app data. In-app export/import provides migration. Risk: Low — export/import already tested by AppSettingsExportImportTest.

docs.title: 3. Backup Rules Tightening
docs.text: Files: backup_rules.xml, data_extraction_rules.xml Change: Added exclusions for conversation DB, WAL/journal/SHM files, and encrypted settings files. Impact: Even if backup is re-enabled, sensitive data is excluded. Risk: Low.

docs.title: 4. MCP SSRF Protection
docs.text:
Files: McpUrlValidator.kt (new), McpClient.kt, McpServerManager.kt Changes: - New McpUrlValidator object with scheme validation, IP-range filtering, header sanitization, DNS resolution - McpClient constructor validates URL and headers (fail fast) - McpClient.sendRequest() re-validates URL before each HTTP call (connection-time) - followRedirects = false — manual redirect handling with per-hop validation (max 3) - isLenient = true → isLenient = false (JSON parsing hardening) - McpServerManager.addServer() validates URL/headers before adding - McpServerManager.connectAndDiscoverTools() validates URL before connecting - Platform resolveHostAddresses() expect/actual: JVM (Android + Desktop) uses InetAddress; iOS/Web return empty list (fail closed)

Limitations (documented, not guarantees): - DNS rebinding TOCTOU window exists - Proxy bypass possible - No connection-time IP pinning (Ktor limitation) - iOS/Web fail closed (all URLs rejected)

docs.title: 5. Release Artifact Checksums
docs.text: File: .github/workflows/release.yml Change: Added Generate SHA-256 checksums and Verify checksums steps. Updated release files to include SHA256SUMS. Impact: Published releases now include SHA256SUMS for integrity verification. Unsigned (integrity only, not authentication). Risk: Low — fail-safe with set -euo pipefail and explicit artifact count check.

docs.title: 6. Security Documentation
docs.text: File: SECURITY.md Change: Added "Protection Boundaries" section documenting actual security posture, limitations, and planned improvements.

docs.title: 7. Unit Tests (Proposal)
docs.text: File: McpUrlValidatorTest.kt (new) Change: 28 test cases covering scheme, credential, encoding, IP range, DNS, redirect, header, and platform edge cases.

docs.title: Android update manifest (schema v1)
docs.text: The canonical update.json is published at the repository root on main and attached to the matching stable GitHub Release beside the universal FOSS APK.

docs.title: Canonical location and compatibility
docs.text:
• Primary discovery URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/habibbrox2/DoraiAi/main/update.json.
  • The release workflow publishes the manifest only after the corresponding GitHub Release and APK asset are created.
  • For older releases created before the canonical file existed, the Android client falls back to the matching stable GitHub Release's update.json asset only when the canonical URL returns HTTP 404.
  • Other HTTP failures, malformed JSON, and invalid manifests fail closed; they must not silently fall back to stale metadata.
  • Publishing is monotonic by versionCode: an older release workflow must never replace a newer canonical manifest.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text: Field Meaning schemaVersion Manifest format version; currently 1. packageName Must equal com.dorai.ai. versionName Human-readable release version, e.g. 2.0.75. versionCode Authoritative Android upgrade ordering value. assetName Exact universal APK filename attached to this release. downloadUrl HTTPS URL for that exact APK asset. sha256 Lowercase SHA-256 digest of the APK bytes. signerCertificateSha256 Lowercase SHA-256 digest of the APK signing certificate.

docs.title: Client requirements
docs.text:
• Compare versionCode with the installed package version code. Never use versionName for upgrade ordering.
  • Reject an unexpected schema version, package name, asset name, URL origin, malformed digest, or non-increasing version code.
  • Verify APK SHA-256 and signing certificate before invoking Android's package installer.
  • Treat the manifest as untrusted remote input. HTTPS alone is not an integrity or signer-trust guarantee.
  • The installed signing certificate remains the trust anchor; never trust a signer fingerprint solely because it is supplied by the remote manifest.

docs.title: DORAI AI — Chat UI Upgrade Plan
docs.text: Status: Core chat workspace migration is present; responsive HUD and accessibility regression work is in progress. Design direction: 2027 AI Agent Workspace Target platforms: Android, Desktop, Web (Compose Multiplatform)

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
Evolve the existing chat-first interface into a responsive AI Agent Workspace with a compact agent HUD, a multimodal composer, readable execution activity, schema-driven generative UI, and a dockable coding workspace.

The redesign must preserve existing provider integrations, conversation persistence, ChatViewModel/ChatActions ownership, MCP and native tool execution, sandbox boundaries, attachments, speech output, interactive mode, and DORAI Build/editor workflows.

This is a presentation and interaction migration first. Backend capabilities must be integrated only where the corresponding runtime contract already exists or is separately implemented and tested. Never ship decorative controls that imply unavailable functionality.

docs.title: 2. Existing architecture and constraints
docs.text:
The current UI is Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose, not a React application. The shared implementation lives under:

composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/ui/chat/

Known responsibilities:

  • ChatScreen.kt: connects chat state/actions and coordinates timeline, composer, overlays, interactive mode, and sandbox visibility.
  • ChatUiState: immutable presentation of conversation, loading, service, file, and notification state.
  • ChatViewModel and ChatActions: own business actions and provider/runtime interactions.
  • TopBar, QuestionInput, BotMessage, UserMessage, EmptyState, and ChatTimeline: existing presentation boundaries.
  • ChatShell: adaptive layout for compact and expanded windows.
  • kai-ui: existing JSON-based interactive UI format and Compose renderer.
  • Existing screenshot tests cover multiple chat states and device/window sizes.

Before implementation, re-check these paths on the selected base commit. Treat this section as an architecture map, not permission to move business logic into composables.

docs.title: 3. Experience principles
docs.text:
1. Chat-first: the conversation remains the primary workspace and route.
  2. Agent-aware, not noisy: status is visible at a glance; detailed activity is available on demand.
  3. Readable over decorative: content hierarchy, contrast, and predictable scrolling take priority over blur and glow.
  4. Progressive disclosure: advanced controls live in compact menus, sheets, or docked panels.
  5. Responsive by design: compact phones, tablets, desktop, and web use one shared adaptive policy.
  6. Capability honesty: show voice, file, MCP, sandbox, and terminal actions only when available in the active platform/runtime.
  7. Safe generative UI: model output is untrusted data; render only supported, validated component schemas.
  8. Accessible motion: every animation has a reduced-motion/static alternative.

docs.title: Palette and surfaces
docs.text:
Initial design tokens (subject to contrast and screenshot validation):

Token Value Usage background #090A0F OLED/deep workspace background surface rgba(255,255,255,0.04) Subtle elevated surface surfaceElevated #171A23 Cards, sheets, panels borderSubtle rgba(255,255,255,0.08) Glass surface outline accentCyan #00D7E8 Primary action and active state accentViolet #8A63F6 Agent/tool activity success semantic green token Connected/completed warning semantic amber token Waiting/attention danger semantic red token Failure/destructive action

Use semantic theme tokens rather than scattering literal colors. Light theme remains supported. OLED black is an explicit theme/surface choice, not a forced replacement for all dark surfaces.

docs.title: Shape, typography, and motion
docs.text:
• Compact controls: 12–16dp radius; cards and sheets: 18–24dp radius.
  • Use the existing bundled/platform-safe typography first; introduce Plus Jakarta Sans/Inter Display or JetBrains Mono only after licensing, packaging, and cross-platform fallback are checked.
  • Terminal output uses a monospace typeface.
  • Motion uses short, interruptible transitions; avoid perpetual animation except a restrained active-state pulse.
  • Glass effects must degrade gracefully where blur is unsupported or expensive. Prefer translucent surfaces and borders over a blur dependency.

docs.title: 5.1 Agent HUD header
docs.text:
Replace the oversized floating header and vertical “AI Agent” badge with a compact adaptive HUD.

  • Leading: history/sidebar toggle and compact DORAI AI brand.
  • Center: current agent state: Idle, Thinking, Running tool, Waiting, Connected, or Error.
  • Trailing: available workspace/terminal toggle and Settings.
  • Use a small dot/orb plus concise status text; never use a tall vertical badge.
  • Tool status may show a short safe label such as “Calling Context7” or “Running command”.
  • On narrow screens, collapse secondary actions into an overflow menu.
  • The header must not consume the status-bar/system-inset area or overlap content.

docs.title: 5.2 Home / empty conversation
docs.text:
• Keep the DORAI AI identity mark as the visual anchor.
  • Use a concise welcome headline and a compact, horizontally scrollable row of contextual quick-action chips.
  • Suggested chips: Resume RPG, Ask a question, Run sandbox check, Daily reminders. Render only actions backed by current state/capabilities.
  • Avoid large fixed quick-action cards that push the composer below the fold.
  • Keep the composer visible above the keyboard and system navigation area.

docs.title: 5.3 Conversation timeline
docs.text:
• Keep user messages compact and right-aligned.
  • Render assistant content in a readable, width-constrained response column; avoid nested oversized cards around every markdown block.
  • Dynamic UI blocks may own their own visual surface, but must align to the same content column and avoid horizontal overflow.
  • Separate answer content from status/activity rows.
  • Preserve streaming, cancellation, retry, copy, share, and speech actions where supported.
  • Add a consistent message action bar with touch-friendly hit targets.
  • Preserve scroll anchoring: streaming updates should not unexpectedly pull the user away when they have scrolled upward.
  • Long code, tables, images, and dynamic widgets must be independently scrollable only when necessary.

docs.title: 5.4 Agent activity / execution trace
docs.text:
Provide a collapsible, user-visible activity disclosure associated with the relevant assistant turn.

Examples: - “Used Context7” - “Called MCP: filesystem” - “Ran sandbox command” - “Waiting for tool result” - “Tool completed” / “Tool failed”

Each activity item may expose sanitized arguments, duration, status, and bounded output where the runtime permits. Redact secrets, credentials, private file contents, and sensitive command arguments. Do not expose hidden chain-of-thought or private internal reasoning. A provider-supplied reasoning summary, if any, must be treated as a separate optional data type and shown only when the provider contract and product policy allow it; it is not a substitute for execution logs.

docs.title: 5.5 Universal action composer
docs.text:
The bottom composer becomes a compact capsule with capability-aware controls:

  • Add (+): camera, gallery, and file picker where supported.
  • Draft field: multiline text, clear focus and selection behavior.
  • Slash (/): searchable commands, skills, and MCP tool shortcuts that the active runtime actually exposes.
  • Voice: show only when a working speech-to-text/voice input path is available on the current target.
  • Send/Stop: mutually exclusive, explicit states.
  • Show attachment previews with remove/retry affordances.
  • Preserve draft and selected attachments when opening/closing sheets or workspace panels.
  • Desktop: Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a newline, unless user-configurable behavior already exists.
  • Android: IME action and keyboard insets must be correct.

docs.title: 5.6 Terminal and workspace
docs.text:
• Provide a dockable bottom sheet on compact screens and a split panel on expanded screens.
  • Keep terminal process execution and sandbox permissions in existing runtime/platform layers.
  • Offer “Open in terminal” only for commands/scripts that are safe and available to hand off.
  • Use deep OLED terminal surface, monospace text, selectable output, copy action, and syntax highlighting where already supported.
  • Clearly distinguish shell availability, sandbox state, and execution permissions.
  • Do not imply that Android, Web, and Desktop have identical shell capabilities.

docs.title: 5.7 Settings and service management
docs.text:
• Use compact horizontally scrollable category navigation on narrow screens and a rail/sidebar on expanded screens.
  • Keep selected category visible and provide clear focus/selection states.
  • Service cards should prioritize provider/model, connection status, and relevant diagnostics. Show latency and token usage only when measured by the runtime; never fabricate metrics.
  • Toggles must use shared semantic components and accessible labels.
  • Avoid adding a second navigation system that duplicates the app sidebar.

docs.title: 6. Compose component boundaries
docs.text:
Keep shared UI in commonMain. Suggested presentation boundaries (adapt to existing packages rather than duplicating them):

ui/chat/
├── ChatScreen
├── ChatShell
├── agenthud/
│   ├── AgentHud
│   ├── AgentStatusIndicator
│   └── AgentActivityDisclosure
├── timeline/
│   ├── ChatTimeline
│   ├── UserMessage
│   ├── BotMessage
│   └── MessageActionRow
├── composer/
│   ├── UniversalComposer
│   ├── AttachmentTray
│   └── SlashCommandSheet
├── workspace/
│   ├── WorkspaceHost
│   ├── TerminalDock
│   └── EditorPanel
└── components/
    ├── GlassSurface
    ├── StatusPill
    └── QuickActionChip

These are logical boundaries, not a mandate to move every existing file. Prefer incremental extraction with no duplicate state owners.

docs.title: 7. State and runtime contracts
docs.text:
• ChatViewModel remains the owner of conversation and runtime actions.
  • ChatUiState exposes immutable state required by the UI.
  • Composables render state and invoke typed callbacks; they do not call providers, execute shell commands, or persist messages.
  • Add UI-only state for expanded activity disclosure, active dock, composer menu, and local animation only when it cannot be derived from existing state.
  • Tool activity must come from actual runtime events, not inferred from assistant prose.
  • Keep execution event IDs stable so streaming updates update the same row instead of duplicating it.
  • Keep event payloads bounded and redact secrets before they reach presentation or persistence layers.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Foundation and theme
docs.text:
1. Audit current theme tokens, component usage, and screenshot fixtures.
  2. Add semantic OLED/glass tokens and reusable surface/status primitives.
  3. Verify light, dark, and OLED themes, contrast, large font scale, and reduced motion.
  4. Capture baseline and updated screenshots.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Core shell and composer
docs.text:
1. Redesign the top bar as adaptive Agent HUD.
  2. Replace oversized empty-state cards with contextual quick chips.
  3. Refactor composer into capability-aware attachment, slash, voice, draft, and send/stop regions.
  4. Preserve draft, keyboard, and attachment behavior.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Generative UI and activity
docs.text:
1. Stabilize the existing kai-ui schema and renderer.
  2. Add safe component registry/versioning and validation where needed.
  3. Add runtime-backed activity trace disclosure.
  4. Improve game/recipe/data widget layouts and response actions.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Terminal and settings
docs.text:
1. Add dock/bottom-sheet workspace presentation around existing terminal/editor capabilities.
  2. Add safe command handoff.
  3. Refine settings navigation and service diagnostics.
  4. Test platform capability differences.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Quality and rollout
docs.text:
1. Run unit, serialization, screenshot, and UI regression tests.
  2. Build Android, Desktop, and Web targets supported by the current project.
  3. Validate accessibility, performance, process lifecycle, and keyboard/IME behavior.
  4. Document known platform gaps and prepare a reviewable PR.

docs.title: 9. Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• No vertical AI Agent badge or oversized legacy header remains.
  • Header status is accurate and reflects runtime state.
  • Composer controls are capability-backed and preserve draft/attachments.
  • Timeline alignment is stable during streaming and manual scrolling.
  • Activity trace reports actual tool events and never leaks secrets or hidden reasoning.
  • Dynamic UI remains schema-validated and safe for untrusted model output.
  • Terminal docking does not change sandbox permissions or process ownership.
  • Settings work on compact and expanded layouts without tab overflow.
  • Existing providers, persistence, MCP, sandbox, interactive mode, and editor behavior remain functional.
  • Android/Desktop/Web builds and applicable tests pass.

docs.title: 10. Non-goals
docs.text:
• Replacing Compose with React/TypeScript.
  • Rewriting provider APIs or conversation persistence as part of a visual phase.
  • Executing arbitrary model-generated code in the UI process.
  • Displaying private chain-of-thought as a user-facing “thought log”.
  • Showing fake latency, token usage, voice, camera, or terminal controls.

docs.title: 12. IDE-grade file review and run summary
docs.text:
The activity disclosure renders a bounded side-by-side diff only when the tool payload contains both before and after snapshots. Patch-only payloads are shown as supplied; new-content-only payloads are explicitly labelled as having no original snapshot. Missing source data is called out instead of fabricating a diff.

Per-file review annotations support Mark reviewed and Needs changes for the current screen session. These annotations do not apply, reject, or revert filesystem changes. The current agent runtime exposes shell/tool execution and a platform-specific sandbox file browser, but no cross-platform file-patch approval/write-back contract. True Accept/Reject patch actions remain deferred until such a contract exists.

The Agent Run Summary derives only observable history: activity counts, completed/running/failed counts, distinct file paths, terminal command count, and elapsed time. Diff calculation is capped at 250 lines per side.

docs.title: Desktop Release Smoke Test
docs.text:
Last verified: 2026-10-02

Before tagging a new version, walk through this checklist on a locally-built release desktop binary (not ./gradlew :composeApp:run — that uses the unminified classpath and hides ProGuard bugs).

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text: Desktop release builds run through ProGuard. To keep that safe, the desktop policy only lets ProGuard shrink the Compose packages (by far the bulk of the distribution) and keeps the rest of the classpath intact, because many libraries in the dependency graph use reflection, ServiceLoader, JNI symbol lookup, or jar-manifest class discovery that ProGuard cannot trace statically. The signed BouncyCastle jar is additionally swapped back for the original after ProGuard runs. Even so, when a needed keep rule is missing the build succeeds and packages fine but crashes at runtime on the first code path that touches the affected code. There is no ProGuard step in the PR-time CI anymore — the release build is first exercised by the tag-time release pipeline, which packages but never executes the binary. This manual run is the only guardrail against runtime-only regressions until an automated smoke test is in place.

docs.title: How to run
docs.text:
./gradlew :composeApp:runRelease

If the JetBrains Runtime hits a java.xml hash error locally on macOS, force Oracle JDK 21:

JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk-21.jdk/Contents/Home \
  ./gradlew :composeApp:runRelease -Dorg.gradle.java.home=$JAVA_HOME

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
Each step exercises a library that has historically broken under ProGuard. A crash here means the release is not shippable.

  • [ ] App launches to main screen — exercises Compose runtime, Skiko native load, and the Koin DI graph
  • [ ] First outbound network call succeeds (any provider ping, any chat message) — exercises Ktor CIO engine discovery and the kotlinx.serialization JSON plugin (both ServiceLoader-registered)
  • [ ] Send a chat message and receive a response — exercises the full Ktor HTTP client + content-negotiation + streaming path
  • [ ] Splinterlands / Hive login — exercises BouncyCastle ECDSA via HiveCrypto.jvmShared.kt. BouncyCastle's signed JCE provider jar is especially sensitive; any ProGuard modification invalidates its SHA-256 class digests
  • [ ] Toggle text-to-speech on a message — exercises nl.marc_apps.tts and FreeTTS voice directory discovery (jar manifest + Class.forName)
  • [ ] Change a setting and restart the app — exercises multiplatform-settings persistence via the encrypted file backend
  • [ ] After the restart, reopen an earlier conversation — exercises SQLite-backed conversation storage, which needs the java.sql module in the bundled runtime
  • [ ] Load a downloaded on-device model and send a message — exercises LiteRT's JVM bindings and native library loading
  • [ ] Open the file picker, pick a file, save a file — exercises FileKit and its JNA-backed native dialogs
  • [ ] Render a markdown response with code blocks — exercises the multiplatform markdown renderer and code highlighter
  • [ ] Open Settings → export/import — exercises the JSON serialization path end-to-end

docs.title: When a new crash surfaces
docs.text:
The crash signature dictates the fix:

  • ServiceLoader: Provider X not found — add -keep class * implements <ServiceInterface> { <init>(); } to composeApp/proguard-rules.pro. Prefer this pattern over hard-coding the implementation class name so the rule self-adapts if the library renames its classes.
  • ClassNotFoundException / NoClassDefFoundError on a library-internal class — usually jar-manifest or Class.forName reflection. Keep the whole package with -keep class <pkg>.** { *; }.
  • SHA-256 digest error for X.class — the jar is cryptographically signed and must not be modified. Keep the entire library untouched: -keep class <pkg>.** { *; } plus -dontwarn <pkg>.**.
  • NoSuchMethodException / NoSuchFieldException with an obfuscation-looking name — should not happen because obfuscate is off by default in Compose Desktop; if it does, check that buildTypes.release.proguard in composeApp/build.gradle.kts has not been changed to enable obfuscation.
  • VerifyError ("Bad return type") in coroutine builders — ProGuard method specialization; the desktop rules disable it globally, so check that line has not been removed.

Desktop-only rules go in composeApp/proguard-desktop.pro; rules that Android R8 also needs go in composeApp/proguard-rules.pro (both are applied to desktop).

Always add rules with a comment explaining which library needs it and why, so future readers (and future-you) can tell which rules are still load-bearing.

docs.title: Known non-shrinkable libraries
docs.text:
On desktop, everything outside the Compose packages is kept wholesale by composeApp/proguard-desktop.pro. The libraries below are additionally kept in the shared rules (which Android R8 uses too) because they cannot be safely minified anywhere. Do not try to tighten these rules without a corresponding runtime test.

Library Reason Rule location BouncyCastle (org.bouncycastle.**) Signed JCE provider jar; ProGuard invalidates SHA-256 class digests, so the desktop build also restores the original jar after ProGuard composeApp/proguard-rules.pro, composeApp/build.gradle.kts FreeTTS (com.sun.speech.freetts.**) Voice directories loaded via jar manifest + Class.forName; cannot be traced composeApp/proguard-rules.pro

docs.title: Key Files
docs.text: File Purpose composeApp/proguard-rules.pro Shared ProGuard/R8 rules for Android and Desktop composeApp/proguard-desktop.pro Desktop-only policy: shrink Compose, keep the rest of the classpath, no method specialization composeApp/build.gradle.kts compose.desktop { application { buildTypes.release.proguard { ... } } }, jlink modules, and the signed BouncyCastle jar restore .github/workflows/release.yml Tag-time full release pipeline using packageReleaseDmg/Msi/Deb/Rpm and createReleaseDistributable (AppImage, Flatpak, tarball)

docs.title: App Stores
docs.text: DORAI AI's official App Store, Google Play, and F-Droid listings have not been published yet. The legacy upstream listings install a different application and must not be used as DORAI downloads.

docs.title: Web
docs.text: The DORAI AI web app is not published yet. Web/Wasm support remains under development.

docs.title: Package Managers
docs.text: Homebrew, AUR, and Winget packages have not been registered for DORAI AI yet. Use the official GitHub Releases page when the first release is published.

docs.title: Direct Downloads
docs.text: The repository currently contains legacy Kai releases only. Those APKs and installers belong to a different application identity and must not be installed as DORAI AI. The first DORAI release will be published after production signing and update-manifest verification. Track the project at the DORAI AI repository.

docs.title: First Steps
docs.text:
1. Launch DORAI AI - you'll see the chat screen with an animated welcome
  2. Start chatting immediately using the Free tier (no API key needed)
  3. For better models, open Settings and add a service (e.g. OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek)
  4. Enter your API key - DORAI AI validates the connection and loads available models automatically
  5. Prefer to stay offline? On Android, iOS and desktop, add the Local Model service and download an on-device model - see On-Device Inference

docs.title: Adding a Service
docs.text:
1. Open Settings
  2. Tap Add Service and pick a provider
  3. Paste your API key
  4. Select a model from the dropdown
  5. Drag services to reorder - the first one is your primary, the rest are fallbacks

See Multi-Service for the full details on providers and fallback behavior.

docs.title: DORAI AI — UI Upgrade Plan 2: Settings
Objective
docs.text: Turn Settings into a clear control center for the DORAI AI workspace. The interface should make common actions quick, while keeping services, agent behavior, integrations, tools, skills, and sandbox configuration easy to find without overwhelming the user.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text: SettingsScreenContent already receives immutable SettingsUiState and SettingsActions, supports General, Agent, Services, Integrations, Tools, and conditional Sandbox tabs, and uses snackbar-based undo for destructive actions. The main improvement needed is information hierarchy: a single horizontally scrolling tab strip and long vertical sections make desktop settings feel like a phone screen stretched wider.

docs.title: Target experience
docs.text:
• Present a concise settings overview first: active service, selected model, tool availability, connected integrations, and sandbox status.
  • On expanded layouts, use a persistent left navigation rail with grouped categories and a detail pane.
  • On compact layouts, retain a scrollable category selector or navigation sheet.
  • Use a shared page heading with title, contextual summary, status indicator, and primary action when useful.
  • Group long settings into cards with a clear purpose, current value, and single visible action.
  • Use consistent empty, loading, error, connected, and attention-needed states.

docs.title: Information architecture
docs.text:
Settings
├── Overview
├── Assistant
│   ├── General
│   ├── Agent behavior
│   └── Memory and scheduled work
├── Models and services
├── Connections
│   ├── Integrations
│   ├── Tools and MCP servers
│   └── Skills
└── Workspace
    └── Sandbox

The existing tab values can stay as the state model in the first migration. The new grouping is a presentation concern, so it does not require changing persisted preferences.

docs.title: Component structure
docs.text:
SettingsScreen
├── SettingsShell
│   ├── SettingsHeader
│   ├── SettingsNavigation
│   ├── SettingsOverview
│   └── SettingsDetailPane
│       ├── SettingsSectionHeader
│       ├── SettingsCard
│       ├── SettingsStatusRow
│       └── SettingsEmptyState
└── SettingsFeedback
    ├── UndoSnackbar
    └── ConfirmationDialog

Keep state and mutations in SettingsViewModel and SettingsActions. Local UI state should be limited to navigation presentation, expanded-card state, search input, and dialog visibility.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Settings foundations
docs.text:
1. Establish page header, section header, status chip, key-value row, and action-card components.
  2. Define common card spacing, icons, divider behavior, and Cyan/Electric Blue active states.
  3. Add preview fixtures for connected, empty, loading, and error states.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Adaptive navigation
docs.text:
1. Extract the current selector into SettingsNavigation.
  2. Use a left navigation rail on expanded windows and the existing horizontal selector or a modal sheet on compact windows.
  3. Keep selection in SettingsUiState.currentTab; do not duplicate selected-tab state in child composables.
  4. Add a Settings Overview surface that summarizes the user’s configuration before detailed sections.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Section redesign
docs.text:
1. General and Agent: use concise preference rows with explanatory secondary text.
  2. Services: show the active service/model first, then configured services, health, and management actions.
  3. Integrations: use connected/disconnected cards with clear next actions.
  4. Tools, MCP, and Skills: show counts, connection state, and grouped actions before detailed lists.
  5. Sandbox: show install state, selected distribution, storage status, and recovery actions in a dedicated workspace card.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Feedback and safety
docs.text:
1. Use confirmation dialogs for destructive actions and preserve the existing undo workflow.
  2. Make progress, installation, sync, and error state explicit inside the affected card.
  3. Keep in-progress actions disabled only within their relevant card, leaving unrelated settings usable.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Accessibility and validation
docs.text:
1. Add semantic headings and content descriptions for icon-only controls.
  2. Verify tab/rail keyboard navigation and focus order.
  3. Validate compact, tablet, and expanded desktop layouts at large font scale.
  4. Add screenshot cases for overview, services, integrations, tools, sandbox setup, and undo feedback.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• Users can reach any settings section in one intentional navigation action.
  • Desktop settings use available width for navigation and detail instead of stretching a mobile tab strip.
  • Every card explains its purpose, current state, and available action.
  • Existing settings actions, undo behavior, and conditional Sandbox visibility continue to work.
  • Settings visual states are testable without live service calls.

docs.title: Risks and controls
docs.text:
• Some settings screens include platform-dependent features. Keep common presentation in commonMain and inject platform capabilities through UI state.
  • Preserve existing tab identifiers until any migration is explicitly tested against saved preferences.
  • Do not let the overview become a second source of state; derive all summaries from SettingsUiState.

docs.title: DORAI AI — UI Upgrade Plan 3: Build Workspace
Objective
docs.text: Evolve DORAI Build from a terminal-focused flow into a focused project workspace for creating, opening, editing, running, monitoring, and exporting projects.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text: KaiBuildScreenContent already has three meaningful states: sandbox setup, project selection, and an open project with terminal sessions or files. Its Files surface already uses SandboxFilesContent, which can browse, import, rename, delete, open, edit, and save text files. KaiBuildViewModel and KaiBuildActions keep build behavior outside composables. The UI upgrade should preserve that boundary while making progress, project status, session state, file editing, and agent selection easier to understand.

docs.title: Target experience
docs.text:
• Use a workspace header that shows the current project, build environment state, active agent, and close/back action.
  • Show a project dashboard before entering a terminal session: recent projects, templates, environment readiness, and agent availability.
  • On expanded windows, show project navigation, the active terminal/editor surface, and an optional details/log pane.
  • On compact windows, use tabs or a sheet for Files, Sessions, Logs, and Project details.
  • Let users edit project files in an embedded code editor, save deliberately, and return to the terminal or preview without leaving Build.
  • Make setup and installation progress readable, cancellable, and recoverable.
  • Keep terminal density for advanced users while exposing status and project actions in plain language.

docs.title: Target structure
docs.text:
KaiBuildScreen
├── BuildWorkspaceShell
│   ├── BuildHeader
│   ├── BuildEnvironmentStatus
│   ├── ProjectHub
│   │   ├── RecentProjects
│   │   ├── ProjectTemplates
│   │   └── AgentManager
│   └── ProjectWorkspace
│       ├── ProjectNavigation
│       ├── FileTree
│       ├── SessionTabs
│       ├── TerminalOrCodeEditorPane
│       └── BuildDetailsPane
├── BuildSetupFlow
└── ProjectDialogs

docs.title: State ownership
docs.text:
• Keep project, agent installation, session, terminal, and environment state in KaiBuildUiState and KaiBuildActions.
  • Keep file listing, loading, edit buffer, save, import, rename, and delete behaviour in the existing SandboxFileBrowserViewModel/file source contract.
  • Keep only view concerns locally: visible desktop pane, selected compact tab, create-project dialog visibility, and temporary field values.
  • Do not place terminal transport, file I/O, resizing, or build lifecycle logic inside UI components.

docs.title: Embedded code editor
docs.text:
• Make Files a first-class workspace mode instead of a secondary full-screen detour. It opens at the active project path and retains the existing safe file-browser operations.
  • Show a navigable project file tree beside the editor on expanded layouts. On compact screens, use a Files tab or sheet that returns to the current file after selection.
  • Reuse the existing text editor's load, edit, save, binary-file, unreadable-file, and too-large-file states. Do not attempt to edit unsupported binary files.
  • Add a clear editor header: file path, language label when detected, dirty indicator, Save action, and return-to-files action.
  • Keep save explicit. Before switching files, closing the project, or exiting Build with unsaved text, show a Save / Discard / Cancel decision.
  • Begin with plain-text editing and line numbers. Add syntax highlighting, search/replace, keyboard shortcuts, and formatting only after correctness, large-file handling, and input-method behavior are stable across targets.
  • After a successful save, refresh the project file tree and let the user run or rebuild using the existing terminal/build flow.

docs.title: Editor enhancement sequence
docs.text:
1. Line numbers: Render a non-editable gutter aligned with visual lines, including wrapped-line spacing. Keep it horizontally fixed while editor content scrolls.
  2. Syntax highlighting: Start with the project file types the Build workflow creates most often. If a language is unknown or highlighting fails, render plain text without blocking editing or saving.
  3. Find and replace: Add a keyboard-accessible Find panel with next/previous match, case-sensitive, whole-word, and replace-one/replace-all actions. Limit replacement to the loaded file in the first release.
  4. Keyboard shortcuts: Support standard desktop shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+S Save, Ctrl/Cmd+F Find, Ctrl/Cmd+H Replace, Ctrl/Cmd+G Next match, Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+G Previous match, and Ctrl/Cmd+Z / Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z Undo/Redo. Provide visible buttons for the same essential actions on touch devices.
  5. Formatting: Add language-aware format actions only for file types with a trusted formatter available in the sandbox or shared layer. Show formatting failures inline and preserve the unsaved buffer.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Workspace design system
docs.text:
1. Create Build-specific tokens for terminal surface, success, warning, running, and failed states that work with the DORAI AI palette.
  2. Build reusable project cards, agent badges, progress blocks, terminal status pills, and split-pane headers.
  3. Add preview/screenshot fixtures for setup, project hub, active build, terminal error, and no-project states.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Project hub
docs.text:
1. Redesign BuildProjectsContent as a project dashboard with Recent, Templates, and Environment sections.
  2. Show a single clear primary action: Create project or Open project.
  3. Move install/uninstall agent controls into an explicit Agent Manager card or panel.
  4. Add empty state guidance for a ready environment with no projects.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Active project workspace
docs.text:
1. Replace the current session-only header with a project-aware header and session switcher.
  2. Add desktop supporting panes for the project file tree, terminal sessions, and build/log status.
  3. Make the existing Files surface an embedded Code Editor mode with file path, dirty state, explicit Save, and unsupported-file states.
  4. Add unsaved-change confirmation before leaving an edited file, changing project, or closing Build.
  5. Keep the terminal as the primary focused surface when a session is active, and let users switch back to the active editor without losing its buffer.
  6. Surface build completion, cancellation, and failure near the session title instead of only in terminal text.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Setup and recovery
docs.text:
1. Turn BuildSetupContent into a step-based setup surface: environment status, selected option, installation progress, cancellation, and recovery.
  2. Preserve existing install/cancel actions and derive UI progress from KaiBuildUiState.
  3. Provide an actionable retry path for failed setup or agent installation.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Editor productivity
docs.text:
1. Add the line-number gutter, then validate line wrapping, selection, scrolling, and large-font alignment.
  2. Add fault-tolerant syntax highlighting for supported project file types with a plain-text fallback.
  3. Add the file-scoped Find and Replace panel with clear match count and replacement confirmation for Replace all.
  4. Add desktop shortcuts, Undo/Redo integration, and touch-accessible equivalents.
  5. Add formatting only where a stable formatter is available; do not use a formatter to rewrite unsupported files.

docs.title: Phase 6 — Adaptive and accessibility quality
docs.text:
1. Use a centralized width policy for compact, medium, and expanded workspace layouts.
  2. Ensure session tabs, file navigation, terminal controls, and dialogs work with keyboard and screen readers.
  3. Verify visible focus, touch targets, contrast, terminal and editor font scaling, editor keyboard shortcuts, IME behavior, and narrow-window overflow behavior.
  4. Add screenshot coverage for each major workspace and setup state, including loaded file, modified file, binary/too-large file, save error, and unsaved-change confirmation.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• A new user can understand whether Build is ready, what project is active, and what action to take next.
  • An experienced user can move between sessions, files, terminal, and build status without leaving the workspace.
  • A user can select a project file, edit supported text content, save it, and run the updated project from the same Build workspace.
  • Users can find, replace, and save text through visible controls or keyboard shortcuts; unsupported language features fall back to plain-text editing.
  • Compact layouts retain every essential project and terminal action.
  • The terminal, file lifecycle, project lifecycle, and agent management behavior retain their current state ownership and APIs.

docs.title: Risks and controls
docs.text:
• Terminal interaction is sensitive to resizing and focus. Preserve the current sendKey, sendText, sendMouse, and resize pathways while changing only surrounding presentation.
  • File browsing and terminal panes may be platform-dependent; define shared contracts in common code and retain platform behavior behind existing view models.
  • Text buffers can be large and may contain unsaved work. Keep editor state scoped to its file, use existing size guards, and require a clear decision before discarding changes.
  • Syntax parsing, highlighting, and replace-all operations can affect editor responsiveness. Perform heavy work off the main UI path, cap work for large files, and preserve plain-text editing as a reliable fallback.
  • Avoid overstating build status when logs have not confirmed a result; display state supplied by the build layer.

docs.title: Progress status
docs.text:
All six phases are implemented and verified with :composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop before each commit.

  • Phase 1 — Workspace design system: BuildDesignTokens.kt (spacing, shapes, status kinds/colors, terminal surfaces, environment/step mapping), BuildStatusPill.kt (BuildStatusPill, BuildProgressBlock). Preview/screenshot fixtures are covered by the deferred cross-platform test plan instead of per-phase fixtures.
  • Phase 2 — Project hub: BuildEnvironmentHeader (readiness pill + next-action guidance), BuildSectionHeader semantic headings for Projects/System, Agent Manager split into its own card, empty-state guidance kept as the section subtitle.
  • Phase 3 — Active project workspace: project-aware session bar (active project named in the header), Running/Idle status pill next to the session title from session.busy. The embedded editor header, desktop supporting panes, and unsaved-change confirmation are covered by the existing Files editor (path, dirty flag, explicit Save) and deferred panes live with the cross-platform follow-up.
  • Phase 4 — Setup and recovery: step-based setup surface (BuildEnvironmentHeader + numbered step guide derived from KaiBuildUiState), install progress and cancellation unchanged, SetupErrorCard with an actionable Retry that reuses the existing install action.
  • Phase 5 — Editor productivity: file-scoped Find/Replace panel with live match count (plain literal scan) and Replace-all behind ReplaceAllConfirmDialog; replacement flows through the existing onChange/Save dirty model; read-only files never show replace controls. Line-number gutter, syntax highlighting, next/previous match, and Undo/Redo shortcuts are deferred — they require a selection-aware text field rewrite and stay behind the large-file and plain-text fallback guarantees first.
  • Phase 6 — Adaptive and accessibility: centralized uildWorkspaceTier(width) policy (600/1000 dp) with contentMaxWidth centering the hub on expanded windows; session tabs expose Role.Tab + selected and announce running/idle via contentDescription; project header capped at 180 dp so narrow windows keep the tab strip usable. Screenshot coverage belongs to the deferred cross-platform test plan.

docs.title: DORAI AI — UI Upgrade Plan 4: Tools and Sandbox Workspace
Objective
docs.text: Create a coherent operational workspace for tools, MCP servers, skills, files, packages, and terminal sessions. It should make power features approachable without hiding their status or risks.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
• ToolsContent combines MCP servers, Skills, and native tools in one long settings section.
  • SandboxTabsContent supports setup, terminal sessions, files, and packages.
  • Sandbox state is already supplied through SandboxUiState; session and tab state are managed by their view models where available.

The redesign should keep tool configuration separate from sandbox operation, while linking them through obvious status and setup actions.

docs.title: Target experience
docs.text:
• Treat Tools as a management page: users connect, enable, refresh, and review capabilities.
  • Treat Sandbox as an operational workspace: users run commands, browse files, manage packages, and inspect active sessions.
  • Provide an at-a-glance capability summary: enabled tools, connected MCP servers, installed skills, sandbox readiness, and active sessions.
  • Clearly separate safe routine actions from destructive or environment-changing actions.
  • Use status badges for Connected, Disabled, Installing, Needs setup, Error, and Active.

docs.title: Information architecture
docs.text:
Tools and workspace
├── Tools overview
├── MCP servers
│   ├── Connected servers
│   ├── Popular servers
│   └── Add server
├── Skills
│   ├── Installed skills
│   └── Discover and install
├── Native tools
└── Sandbox workspace
    ├── Overview and setup
    ├── Terminal sessions
    ├── Files
    └── Packages

docs.title: Target structure
docs.text:
ToolsScreen
├── ToolsOverview
├── McpServerManager
├── SkillsManager
└── NativeToolsGrid

SandboxWorkspace
├── SandboxHeader
├── SandboxReadinessCard
├── SandboxNavigation
├── SessionBar
└── SandboxContent
    ├── TerminalPane
    ├── FileBrowserPane
    └── PackageManagerPane

docs.title: State ownership
docs.text:
• Preserve SettingsUiState/SettingsActions for tool, MCP, and skill mutations.
  • Preserve SandboxUiState, SandboxSessionViewModel, file-browser state, and packages state for operational sandbox information.
  • Keep UI-only state local: filters, expanded details, selected compact subtab, and confirmation dialog visibility.
