docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
• Read index.md for scope and layering (runtime vs knowledge).
  • Read selection-policy.md before adding or dropping a row.
  • Do not add live MCP probes to production code.

docs.title: 1. Read the current list
docs.text: Read composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/mcp/PopularMcpServers.kt (popularMcpServers) and the Current set in servers.md.

docs.title: 2. Probe each URL
docs.text:
For every current row, POST Streamable HTTP like the app client (McpClient):

  1. initialize — protocol 2024-11-05, empty capabilities, clientInfo name DORAI AI.
  2. notifications/initialized.
  3. tools/list.

Headers: Content-Type: application/json, Accept: application/json, text/event-stream. Forward Mcp-Session-Id when present. Accept a JSON body or an SSE data: line.

Record: HTTP status, initialize ok/fail, tools/list ok/fail, tool names (or count), error text. Timeout ~15s; retry once on timeout or 5xx.

Auth-optional rows (Jina AI): probe without a key. Initialize success is enough.

docs.title: 3. Diff and apply
docs.text:
1. Diff probe results against the Current set and against Kotlin. Show kept / dropped / probe-failed before writing.
  2. Drop only rows the policy says must drop (dead, not MCP, paid initialize, non-retryable origin 526/530).
  3. Do not add new hosts unless product explicitly expands the list.
  4. Update runtime list in:

composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/mcp/PopularMcpServers.kt

Preserve PopularMcpServer field order, comments, and helper functions. Update descriptions only when the probe shows they are wrong. 5. If the one-tap list changed, update the server table in README.md and the Popular Servers paragraph in docs/features/mcp.md. 6. Update this bundle: - Replace the Current set and probe table in servers.md - Set generated: { by: process:update-popular-mcp-servers, at: <ISO-8601 UTC> } - Set stale_after to ~14 days ahead (YYYY-MM-DD) - After tests pass, set verified 7. Append a dated entry to log.md (newest first under today’s heading).

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
1. ./gradlew :composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop
  2. ./gradlew :composeApp:desktopTest --tests '*PopularMcpServers*'
  3. ./gradlew spotlessApply
  4. Update PopularMcpServersTest.kt only if a fixture name/URL used by tests changed.
  5. On green tests, set on servers.md:

verified: { by: process:desktopTest-PopularMcpServers, at: <ISO-8601 UTC> }

docs.title: Hard rules
docs.text:
• Do not add runtime network calls to decide which popular servers to show.
  • Do not drop a row on a single timeout or 5xx (retry, then keep and mark failed).
  • Do not add new hosts without an explicit product decision.
  • Bundle and Kotlin must not drift: every refresh updates both.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: The Settings → Tools add-server sheet should only one-tap endpoints that a user can reach without paying, over Streamable HTTP, and that still speak MCP.

docs.title: Must hold (all of them)
docs.text:
1. Transport — HTTPS Streamable HTTP (POST with Content-Type: application/json and Accept: application/json, text/event-stream). No stdio.
  2. Price — free to add. An optional free API key is allowed (Jina AI). Paid-only hosts stay out.
  3. Usefulness — a real end-user job (docs, search, weather, transit, …), not a demo echo server.
  4. Probe — attested live, or kept under the timeout rule below.

docs.title: Attested live
docs.text:
A server is attested live when a probe matching the app client succeeds:

  1. initialize with protocol 2024-11-05, empty capabilities, clientInfo.name = "DORAI AI".
  2. notifications/initialized (no response required).
  3. tools/list returns a JSON-RPC result (zero tools is unusual — treat as review, not an automatic drop).

Forward Mcp-Session-Id when the host sends one. Parse either a JSON body or an SSE data: line.

Auth-optional hosts (requiresAuth: true): initialize without a key is enough. tools/list may be empty or return an auth error; do not drop for that.

docs.title: Must drop
docs.text:
• DNS failure, connection refused, 404, 410, or a response that is not JSON-RPC MCP.
  • A host that now requires a paid key for initialize itself (401/403 on initialize for a previously no-auth entry).
  • Anything that is not Streamable HTTP.
  • Non-retryable origin failure — Cloudflare/edge 526 (invalid origin TLS), 530 (origin DNS), or a 5xx body that says retryable: false / owner_action_required. Users cannot one-tap these.

docs.title: Must not drop on one flake
docs.text: Timeouts and retryable 5xx: retry once. If the retry still fails, keep the row and mark the probe as failed. Do not remove a previously live server because this machine had a bad network moment.

docs.title: Must not add
docs.text:
• New hosts without an explicit product decision (this list is curated, not scraped).
  • stdio, OAuth-only, or paid-only servers.
  • Duplicates of an existing host (Jina /v1 and /sse are the same host).

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: Only Jina AI is requiresAuth: true today. Do not invent default secret headers. Existing user headers are never overwritten at runtime.

docs.title: Dead hosts already removed
docs.text: remote.mcpservers.org Fetch and Sequential Thinking were dropped earlier (dead). Do not add them back.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
Include a host when all of the following hold (see selection-policy.md):

  1. HTTPS Streamable HTTP MCP (initialize + tools/list like the app client).
  2. Free to add (optional free API key allowed).
  3. A real end-user job, not a demo echo server.

A probe is attested live only when that initialize + tools/list handshake succeeds. Auth-optional hosts (Jina AI) need initialize without a key.

Replace this snapshot only via the refresh playbook.

docs.title: Cloudflare Workers AI
docs.text: DORAI AI exposes Cloudflare Workers AI as a provider using Cloudflare's account-scoped API.

docs.title: Provider configuration
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Services → Cloudflare Workers AI.
  2. Enter the 32-character Cloudflare Account ID in Cloudflare Account ID.
  3. Add a Cloudflare API token with the Workers AI Read permission to discover models and invoke Workers AI.
  4. Refresh the model list. Model IDs are retained exactly as returned by Cloudflare (for example, @cf/...).

The Account ID is stored in the existing provider base-URL setting for backwards-compatible persistence. It is not a URL. The API token is stored through the existing provider credential mechanism; do not commit it or include it in logs.

docs.title: API endpoints
docs.text:
• Chat: POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/ai/v1/chat/completions
  • Model discovery: GET https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/ai/models/search?page={page}&per_page=100

Model discovery parses Cloudflare's v4 result / result_info envelope rather than assuming an OpenAI data array. Results are paginated (up to 20 pages per refresh) and de-duplicated by model ID.

docs.title: Cloudflare AI Gateway
docs.text: This provider entry targets direct Workers AI. It does not currently configure an AI Gateway ID or route third-party models through AI Gateway. Those are distinct endpoint and routing modes and must not be configured by pasting a gateway ID into the Account ID field.

docs.title: Cloudflare MCP
docs.text:
The curated MCP entry points to https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. Select it from the popular MCP list and enter a Cloudflare API token in the Authorization field. The token is sent as a Bearer token. Use the minimum Cloudflare permissions required by the MCP tools you intend to enable.

The MCP client first probes the stateless MCP 2026-07-28 protocol using server/discover. When supported, every request includes the protocol-version header and required per-request metadata; older servers fall back to the legacy initialize handshake.

Skills discovery is attempted only when the server advertises the io.modelcontextprotocol/skills extension: - skills/list discovers published skill metadata and follows pagination cursors. - skills/get confirms the metadata and resource manifest for a skill URI. - resources/read retrieves the skill document.

The extension conventionally uses skill:// URIs but can advertise other URI schemes; the server's skills/get response is authoritative. Reading content does not approve or activate a skill. DORAI AI currently does not verify the returned resource digests, so remote metadata and content must remain untrusted and be reviewed before use; embedded scripts are never executed automatically.

The MCP client does not implement Cloudflare's interactive OAuth login. Cloudflare supports API tokens as Bearer credentials for CI/CD and automation, so configure a scoped API token explicitly.

docs.title: Cloudflare Skills marketplace
docs.text: The Skills browser includes the official cloudflare/skills GitHub repository. Skills are fetched from its skills/ root through the existing GitHub marketplace installer. Review skill contents and any bundled scripts before enabling them.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Unit tests cover the Cloudflare response envelope, pagination metadata, invalid response shapes, Account ID validation, and the curated MCP authentication preset.

docs.title: Keyless Auto Fallback Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Route the built-in Free tier through a hidden keyless Kilo/OpenCode fallback exposed as the Auto model alias when no configured provider can answer.

Architecture: Add a focused common-code fallback component that owns the auto alias and ordered keyless provider/model targets. Wire normal chat to try configured services first and always use the hidden fallback after failures; show one Auto Free entry in chat and exclude Kilo and OpenCode from user-facing service selection while retaining provider metadata for internal requests. Update the multi-service behavior spec and add focused common tests.

Tech Stack: Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, kotlinx.coroutines, commonTest.

Spec: User request in this conversation; repository behavior reference: docs/features/multi-service.md.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Keep all shared fallback behavior in composeApp/src/commonMain/; do not use JVM-only APIs.
  • Preserve the configured provider ordering and existing provider request behavior.
  • Keep Kilo and OpenCode available to internal request dispatch but hide them from user-facing service selection; hide legacy entries without deleting persisted settings.
  • Do not add dependencies or change provider credentials; keyless targets must send no API key.
  • Auto fallback is unconditional after configured-provider failures; the previous Free fallback preference does not disable it.
  • Update the relevant feature spec and its Last verified date.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• No configured providers: the built-in Free path must use the Auto alias and try the internal free targets.
  • Configured providers succeed: return their response without invoking hidden targets.
  • Configured providers fail: always continue to Auto, without exposing Kilo/OpenCode in UI/status.
  • All keyless targets fail: surface the final provider error rather than an empty/success-shaped response.
  • A provider failure after tool side effects must not replay the tool loop and duplicate those effects.
  • Legacy saved Kilo/OpenCode instances must not reappear in user-facing service selection.

docs.text:

Interfaces: - Produces internal const val AUTO_MODEL_ID = "auto" and an ordered, typed list of internal targets, each containing a Service and its actual upstream free model ID. - The first target uses Kilo's kilo-auto/free; OpenCode targets use only the free model IDs already declared for OpenCode in Service.kt. - The helper does not expose targets as configured service instances and does not read or persist API keys.

Assert the alias is exactly auto, Kilo is first with model kilo-auto/free, every subsequent OpenCode model is in its declared free-model set, and no paid model appears.

  • [ ] Step 2: Run the focused test and verify it fails

  • [ ] Step 3: Implement the internal target list

Create the focused common-code component and keep the provider/model mapping in this new file, as requested.

  • [ ] Step 4: Run the focused test and verify it passes

Run: .\gradlew.bat :composeApp:desktopTest --tests "com.dorai.ai.data.KeylessFreeTierFallbackTest" Expected: BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

docs.title: Task 2: Route Free chat through Auto and fallback on provider failure
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/data/RemoteDataRepository.kt - Modify: composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/ui/chat/ChatViewModel.kt - Modify: composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/ui/settings/ServicesSettings.kt - Test: composeApp/src/commonTest/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/data/KeylessFreeTierFallbackTest.kt - Test: composeApp/src/commonTest/kotlin/com/dorai/ai/ui/chat/ChatViewModelExtendedTest.kt

Interfaces: - Consumes the ordered targets and AUTO_MODEL_ID from Task 1. - Keep provider dispatch on the existing askWithService/plainChat path; allow the internal target's upstream model ID to override settings-derived credentials without changing saved user settings. - Use FallbackStatus with a public Free/Auto label only; never report internal target names.

  • [ ] Step 1: Add failing fallback-flow tests

Cover: no configured provider invokes Kilo with kilo-auto/free; Kilo failure tries OpenCode free targets in order; a configured provider success does not invoke fallback; fallback exhaustion propagates the final error; no API key is supplied to hidden targets.

  • [ ] Step 2: Run the focused test and verify it fails

Run: .\gradlew.bat :composeApp:desktopTest --tests "com.dorai.ai.data.KeylessFreeTierFallbackTest" Expected: FAIL because chat does not dispatch through the hidden router.

docs.title: Premium Dark Home Screen Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Make the compact empty-chat screen visually match the supplied premium dark DORAI AI reference while preserving the existing Kotlin Multiplatform chat runtime and capability gates.

Architecture: Keep ChatScreen as the owner of UI state, navigation, draft persistence, and side-panel behavior. Build the premium dark presentation from Compose-native backdrop, semantic colors, and existing header/empty-state/composer composables; retain the existing ChatActions, QuestionInput, drawer, sandbox, and service/model selection integrations rather than creating duplicate state or mock workflows.

Tech Stack: Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, Material 3, Compose Resources, Paparazzi screenshot tests, JUnit.

Spec: Supplied c45f6a59-96a8-47c7-957c-3fe8245f96b9.png dark reference; docs/chat-ui-upgrade-plan.md; docs/ui-upgrade-plan-7-premium-chat.md; docs/features/dynamic-ui.md; docs/features/reasoning.md.

docs.title: Visual Comparison Report
docs.text: Area Current mobile-1.png Target reference Implementation decision Canvas Flat grey-to-dark gradient Obsidian canvas with deep cyan/violet waves and controlled neon edges Compose-native dark ambient backdrop; no bitmap/CSS dependency. Header Compact dark HUD with many small controls Floating navy glass bar, clear clusters, status label, terminal and settings actions Restyle AgentHud; retain all existing callbacks and hide non-fitting optional controls behind existing capability gates. Hero Dark square BK monogram Cyan/violet circular orb with orbital light trails and prominent welcome hierarchy Create a lightweight animated orb with a reduced-motion static fallback; derive state from real runtime flags. Actions Wide dark cards with two-line Bengali copy One-line, horizontally scrollable illuminated glass chips Keep only supported prompt/capability actions and retain onQuickStart; do not invent tools. Composer Dark static input Floating dark-glass action bar with attachment, slash/voice, and cyan send affordances Re-skin existing QuestionInput; preserve its attachments, slash completion, draft, keyboard inset, send/cancel semantics. Continuation / bottom navigation Not present in current empty-chat route Reference contains fictional RPG metrics and five destinations Do not render fake progress or cosmetic navigation. Add only after verified saved-game data and application navigation contracts are supplied.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• The supplied premium dark image is the visual source of truth; the existing dark/OLED plans remain behavioral and security constraints.
  • Keep portable UI in commonMain; do not introduce JVM, Android, CSS, or new dependency requirements.
  • Preserve ChatUiState/ChatActions ownership, attachment handling, slash command sourcing, provider selection, sandbox approval gates, dynamic-UI safety, and reasoning privacy behavior.
  • Status, task history, tools, and navigation may be shown only when backed by actual application state; never fabricate RPG metrics, “all systems ready”, tools, or activity.
  • Respect prefersReducedMotion(), Material accessibility semantics, 48dp touch targets, font scaling, contrast, and compact/medium/expanded ChatAdaptivePolicy behavior.
  • Preserve the pre-existing unrelated edit in iosApp/Configuration/Config.xcconfig.
  • Do not run the write-capable screenshot-update workflow; use focused record/verify commands only after inspecting available Gradle tasks.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Dark theme: all home-screen foreground text, borders, and icons remain readable against the new ambient backdrop.
  • Compact width: header clusters never overlap or clip at the Pixel 9a screenshot width and action chips remain reachable by horizontal scrolling.
  • Runtime state: HUD/orb color and label describe only actual idle/generating/speaking/sandbox states.
  • Composer: draft text, file attachments, slash suggestions, keyboard insets, and streaming cancellation survive the visual refactor.
  • Reduced motion: the orb/status effects render a stable, useful fallback when motion is disabled.

docs.title: Self-Review
docs.text:
• Spec coverage: The plan covers the reference’s ambient dark canvas, HUD, orb/title, quick actions, and composer. It deliberately excludes fake continuation metrics and bottom navigation because no verified state or navigation contract exists.
  • Step scan: Each task has a focused test/baseline, implementation action, and validation command; no task introduces a duplicate state owner.
  • Type consistency: ChatScreenContent and QuestionInput retain their existing contracts; new backdrop/orb APIs are presentation-only and receive real booleans from ChatScreen.
  • Review focus: Compact layout, dark contrast, runtime-status truthfulness, composer preservation, and reduced motion are assigned to screenshot/unit validation in Tasks 1–6.
  • Proportion: This plan limits the first delivery to the supplied empty-chat mobile reference; broader dashboard/navigation/game functionality requires a separate product decision and plan.
